we_do_better: Techniques vs. tools distinction — Skills (methods) and Tools (products) are separate tabs; no competitor makes this split, which is uniquely valuable for AI practitioners
Source transparency — video quality badges, low-quality flags, endorsement counts, and source video links let users judge credibility; competitors show no provenance
MCP/connector tracking — dedicated Connectors tab covering 78 MCP servers is a niche no competitor addresses at this depth
Self-improving system and open audit trail (merge log, deleted skills, suggestion queue) — competitors are static catalogs
Knowledge depth — 413 skills, 695 tools, 78 connectors quality-scored, vs competitors' unscored flat lists
Breadth of news sources — 50+ authoritative RSS feeds merged with video-sourced news in one view
Fully free, open-source, no ads, no paywall; model rankings with category podiums no competitor matches
they_do_better: Visual thumbnails and tool logos — Future Tools, Product Hunt AI, Toolify show product images and gradient category headers; our card list is slower to scan and visually undifferentiated
Simultaneous multi-axis filtering — Toolify lets users filter by category + pricing + rating at once; we only support one filter at a time
Sort controls — Future Tools, Hugging Face, Papers with Code all offer newest/most-popular/top-rated sorting; our Skills and Tools tabs have fixed quality-score ordering with no user control
Item-count badges per category — Future Tools and TAAFT display per-filter counts so users know scope before clicking; we show none
Trending / 'what's new' surfacing — all top competitors have a featured/new/trending section; we have no 'freshest additions' view
User-generated signals — Product Hunt shows upvotes; TAAFT shows user saves; Hugging Face shows downloads; our popularity is editorial (endorsement video counts) only
Search UX — Perplexity and DevDocs show live search suggestions; ours requires a submit step
Mobile layout — most competitors are fully mobile-native with touch-friendly card grids; our layout is column-constrained on small screens
borrow_next: Add color-coded left-border to skill/tool cards by score band (green ≥8, amber 6–7, grey <6) — one CSS rule per band, gives instant visual quality-ladder with zero images needed; this is the single highest-leverage professional_design step pending
Add item-count badges to tab nav buttons after data loads (e.g. 'Skills (413)', 'Tool Rating (695)') — ~10 lines of JS from loaded JSON arrays, not stale status.json
Add a sort toggle (Quality | Mentions | Newest) to Skills and Tools tabs — ~20 lines of client-side JS; closes the biggest UX gap vs Toolify and Future Tools for power users

findings.detail: TODAY = datetime(2026, 6, 3, tzinfo=timezone.utc) is hardcoded at module level. compute_age_months() uses this frozen date. As of 2026-06-20, this is now 17 days stale (was 10 days at last review), growing daily. All recency penalties computed by analyze_batch.py are systematically underestimating video ages, causing newer videos to receive lower-than-correct quality scores.
findings.suggestion: Replace with datetime.now(timezone.utc) computed inside compute_age_months() at call time, not at module level.

findings.detail: load_json (L153) and save_json (L161) open files with bare open() — no encoding='utf-8'. Hebrew transcripts and Unicode tool names will cause UnicodeDecodeError/UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 locale runners. src/fetch.py uses encoding='utf-8' consistently; analyze_batch.py does not. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to every open() call in load_json (L153) and save_json (L161). Also fix the remaining bare open() calls at lines 402, 725-726, 729, 732, 747.

findings.detail: process_video.py has duplicated load_json/save_json (L19, L26) with the same missing encoding='utf-8' as analyze_batch.py. _write_skill_md() (L318) also opens SKILL.md output with bare open(). All three fail on Hebrew-sourced or Unicode-named content. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to load_json, save_json, and _write_skill_md in process_video.py. Consolidate load_json/save_json into a shared src/utils.py to prevent divergence recurring.

findings.detail: Transcript failure rate is still 100% — the latest run_report shows no_transcript=38, new_found=38 (100%). The broad except-all in fetch_transcript() silently swallows all failures. The daily news feed now has 22 non-empty entries (improved from 100% empty last cycle), but this is because the analyze stage generated summaries from description text — the underlying transcript pipeline is still broken for all new videos. Weekly (75%) and monthly (83%) summaries remain largely empty.
findings.suggestion: Log the caught exception at WARNING before falling back. Add a health flag: if no_transcript/new_found > 0.5, set status['transcript_health']='degraded' and show an amber dashboard banner. Verify youtube-transcript-api version compatibility.

findings.detail: describe_tool() still exists and returns hardcoded category-keyed strings. Only 8 of 695 tools (1.1%) now have template descriptions — a massive improvement from 10.6% last review because the CLAUDE.md path ran on the bulk of videos. But describe_tool() is still present and will re-infect the catalog on any analyze_batch.py run that falls back to this code path.
findings.suggestion: Replace describe_tool() with transcript-based extraction: use the 1–2 sentences from the video that most concisely describe what the tool does. If no qualifying sentence, set description to null and show 'Description not yet extracted' in the dashboard.

findings.detail: 'Anthropic' is catalogued as a tool. Anthropic is the company, not a product. Still unfixed after 3 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'anthropic' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into the 'claude' tool entry. Already queued as suggestion b9bfdaf0ef.

findings.detail: 'Openai' (incorrect casing, should be 'OpenAI') is catalogued as a tool. OpenAI is the company; ChatGPT, GPT-4, etc. are its products and already have separate entries. Still unfixed after 3 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'openai'/'Openai' tool entry; fold its endorsement_video_ids into 'chatgpt'. Already queued as suggestion b9bfdaf0ef.

findings.where: data/tools.json — 8 of 695 entries (1.1%) have template descriptions
findings.detail: GREATLY IMPROVED: template description rate fell from 10.6% (33/312) to 1.1% (8/695) because the CLAUDE.md analyze path ran on the bulk of videos. The absolute count dropped from 33 to 8. Downgraded from high to low severity. Root cause (describe_tool() in analyze_batch.py) is still present and will re-infect on any analyze_batch.py code path run.
findings.suggestion: Fix describe_tool() in src/analyze_batch.py (see e5a3f8b2c7). The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module can back-fill the remaining 8 template descriptions where transcripts are available.

findings.detail: analyze_batch.py still generates skill records with three hollow template fields: use_case ('Using {tool} for {category} tasks.'), output ('{tool} produces {category}-focused outputs.'), and relevance ('{tool} is featured as an AI tool in this video.'). The CLAUDE.md analyze path generates real content, but if analyze_batch.py runs it will inject filler. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Extract use_case and relevance from the transcript. If no qualifying sentence is found, use null/empty rather than a template string.

findings.detail: PARTIALLY FIXED: daily_news.json is now 100% filled (22 entries, 0 empty) — a major win. However, weekly_news.json still has 149/199 empty summaries (75%) and monthly_news.json has 598/720 empty (83%). The backlog of no-transcript videos (100% failure rate) is not being back-filled in these views. Returning visitors to the News tab still see majority-blank entries for weekly and monthly windows.
findings.suggestion: The improve stage's fill_missing_summaries module must prioritize the weekly and monthly backlog — generate 1-sentence summaries from description text for entries with empty summary. Even 'Video about {tools_found}: {title}' is better than blank. Also address the 100% transcript failure root cause (finding 8a1b5c4d6e).

findings.detail: MCP connector detection uses a hardcoded list of only 8 specific string patterns (filesystem, browser, github, postgres, sqlite, memory, slack, google drive). Any other MCP server mentioned in a video is silently ignored. CLAUDE.md Step 8 specifies exhaustive MCP hunting — this code path misses the vast majority. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Broaden detection: capture any pattern matching 'npx .+-mcp', 'uvx .+-mcp', 'mcpServers', 'smithery', or 'mcp.so' in the text as a generic MCP connector, extracting the name from the matched string.

findings.detail: Slash-command regex r'/[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,20}\b' matches URL path segments (/api, /v1), prose slashes, and file paths. The exclusion list only blocks 14 single-character tokens. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add a context requirement: only record a slash command if it appears adjacent to known AI tool names or a command-demonstration phrase. Extend blocklist to path prefixes (/api, /v1, /v2, /src, /static, /docs).

findings.detail: The tool is still stored as 'Chatgpt' (wrong casing) instead of the correct brand name 'ChatGPT'. This is the most-mentioned tool in the catalog and the casing error appears for every visitor. Already queued as suggestion 253d755074. Still unfixed after 3 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: Rename name to 'ChatGPT' in data/tools.json. Suggestion 253d755074 is already queued — approve it.

findings.detail: fetch_playlist_videos calls request.execute() with no retry or error handling for YouTube API quota exhaustion (HttpError 429/503). If quota is hit mid-pagination (1495+ items across ~30 pages), the function raises an unhandled exception. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Wrap request.execute() in a retry loop with exponential backoff for 429/503, up to 3 attempts, before re-raising.

findings.detail: write_skill_md() (L402) opens SKILL.md output with bare open() — no encoding='utf-8'. main() opens pending JSON files (L725, 747) and sorted_pending cache (L729, 732) without encoding. Hebrew content or Unicode tool names will cause UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 runners. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add encoding='utf-8' to all bare open() calls in analyze_batch.py: lines 402, 725, 729, 732, 747.

findings.detail: In git_commit_push(), the retry loop calls git pull without checking its return code. If pull fails (merge conflict, auth failure), code continues and retries push on a broken state. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Check the return code of git pull: if pr2.returncode != 0, log stderr and return early.

findings.detail: Tab buttons show no item count (e.g. 'Skills (413)', 'Tool Rating (695)'). Competitors (Future Tools, TAAFT) display per-category counts so users know scope before clicking. The counters strip shows correct totals (413 skills from health.json), but nav buttons are bare labels. Still unfixed after 3 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: After loading each tab's data in init(), inject item counts into nav button labels from loaded JSON array lengths. ~10 lines of JS. Already queued as suggestion 3693c44f40.

findings.detail: Skills and Tools tabs have no user-controlled sort. Users can filter by category and toggle multi-tool/low-quality, but cannot sort by newest, most-mentioned, or reverse quality. All benchmark competitors offer multi-axis sort. Still unfixed after 3 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: Add a sort <select> or pill-toggle above each card list: Quality (default) | Mentions | Newest. Client-side sort on the already-loaded array. ~20 lines of JS. Already queued as suggestion 72e04d9c61.

findings.detail: Inline Python in both workflows uses datetime.datetime.utcnow() (lines 153, 196 in analyze.yml; line 125 in review.yml) which is deprecated in Python 3.12+ and may hard-error in Python 3.13+. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Replace datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + 'Z' with datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() in both workflow inline scripts.

findings.detail: renderAlert sets el.innerHTML = msg where msg mixes hardcoded HTML tags with esc(status.token_hint). The esc() call protects the dynamic value, but the innerHTML pattern is fragile — a future maintainer adding a dynamic field may forget esc(). Data comes from repo-committed JSON (low external risk), but the pattern is worth fixing as a matter of hygiene. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Build the alert using DOM methods (createElement, textContent) rather than innerHTML, or create a dedicated safe-template function that always escapes dynamic values.

findings.detail: main() always sorts pending records newest-first (reverse=True at L728), ignoring any order instruction from the workflow. The analyze.yml workflow specifies oldest_first for normal runs but analyze_batch.py has no --order parameter and hard-codes the sort direction. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add an --order argument to analyze_batch.py (default 'oldest_first'). Sort ascending when oldest_first. Pass the workflow's order value via arg or env var.

findings.detail: /tmp/sorted_pending.json is never deleted on startup. If a GitHub Actions runner is reused for back-to-back analyze jobs (warm runners), the file from a previous run persists and newly added pending videos are absent from the sorted list. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Delete /tmp/sorted_pending.json unconditionally at the start of main() before the existence check, so each invocation rebuilds from current disk state.

findings.detail: status.json counters are stale and worsening: total_skills=318 vs actual 413 (−95 gap, up from −38 last review); total_tools=600 vs actual 695 (−95 gap, up from −22); total_connectors=67 vs actual 78 (−11 gap). The dashboard counter strip now reads from health.json (accurate) rather than status.json, so the visual display is correct. However, status.json is still used in run_report tables and as fallback, and the growing gap will mislead any consumer reading status.json directly.
findings.suggestion: Two-part fix (unchanged): (1) Remove total_skills/total_tools/total_connectors from fetch.py's status.update() block. (2) In the analyze stage, update these counters after each file is saved. For now, health.json is the reliable source; document that status.json is fetch-stage-only for these counters.

findings.detail: fetch.py still resets status['total_skills'] (and total_videos_analyzed line 648) to pre-analyze counts on every run. Since fetch runs first and analyze runs after, these counters are always one full fetch cycle stale. Dashboard now reads health.json first, masking the symptom, but the root cause is unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Remove total_skills (and similarly total_tools, total_connectors if present) from the status.update() block in fetch.py. Let the analyze stage or health.py own these counters exclusively.

findings.detail: cu_state = json.load(open(cu_path, encoding='utf-8')) opens the file without a context manager (no with statement), so the file descriptor is never explicitly closed. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Wrap in a with statement: with open(cu_path, encoding='utf-8') as fh: cu_state = json.load(fh).

findings.detail: key = f"{display_name}|" is assigned and never read. Dead code. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Delete line 550 (key = f"{display_name}|"). No other change needed.

findings.detail: Quick-read mode hides ALL .card .sub elements globally (line 305). On the Connectors tab this removes the provider/category/source line essential for evaluating a connector. On the News tab it removes the source name and date. REVIEW.md requires Quick-read to condense uniformly across every tab. Still unfixed.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit exceptions: .newscard .sub and .connectors-card .sub (or a .no-qr-hide class) so only skill/tool card subtitles are hidden in quick-read mode. Connectors and News sub-lines should remain visible.

findings.detail: index.json covers 350 of 413 valid skills (85% — improved from 55% last review). However, 114 skills are still unindexed (up from 94 last review), and 51 phantom slugs remain. The 114 unindexed skills are mostly from recent CLAUDE.md runs. If analyze_batch.py processes a video whose skill slug matches one of these 114, it will see the slug as 'absent' in index and APPEND A DUPLICATE record to skills.json, causing data corruption.
findings.suggestion: On main() startup, reconcile in one pass: (1) drop phantom keys (in index but not in skills.json); (2) ADD all missing valid slugs to the index. Loop through skills_data['skills']: for each skill not in index_data, add its {score, video_quality_score, starred, target_tool} fields. Re-save index.json. Then re-save.

findings.detail: All skill and tool cards use identical visual styling regardless of quality rank, category, or score. A quality-9 skill looks exactly like a quality-3 skill — the score badge is the only differentiator, and it's easy to miss in a long list. Competitors (Future Tools, Product Hunt AI, Hugging Face) use visual tiering, gradient category headers, and thumbnail images. The dashboard is identified in config.json as a top-3 priority for professional_design but no concrete visual differentiation has been applied in 2 review cycles.
findings.suggestion: This cycle's concrete step: add a 3px colored left-border to skill/tool cards by score band — green for score ≥8, amber for 6–7, grey for <6. Requires adding three CSS rules only (no JS). Gives the card list an instant quality-ladder look. Previously proposed in borrow_next — still not applied.

top_actions: Fix the weekly/monthly news backlog (75% and 83% empty summaries): implement fill_missing_summaries in the improve stage to generate 1-sentence summaries from description text for all entries without a summary. Daily news is now working — apply the same fix to the weekly/monthly backlog. Also fix the TODAY hardcoded date in analyze_batch.py:20 (now 17 days stale) so recency penalties are accurate going forward.

Fix the index.json dual problem (51 phantoms + 114 unindexed skills = data corruption risk): on main() startup, reconcile in one pass — drop phantom keys AND add all missing valid skill slugs. Without this, analyze_batch.py will create duplicate skill records for 114 slugs on its next run. This is the highest-risk open bug in the engine.

Add encoding='utf-8' to ALL remaining bare open() calls in analyze_batch.py (L153, 161, 402, 725, 729, 732, 747) and process_video.py (L19, 26, 318) — these are high-severity data corruption bugs on non-UTF-8 runners processing Hebrew transcripts or Unicode tool names.

Apply the one professional_design step this cycle: add a 3px colored left-border to skill/tool cards by score band (green ≥8, amber 6–7, grey <6) — 3 CSS rules only, closes the biggest visual gap vs competitors and gives the card list an instant quality hierarchy.

Quick data fixes already queued (approve them): (1) fix ChatGPT casing in tools.json (suggestion 253d755074); (2) remove Anthropic and Openai company-as-tool entries (suggestion b9bfdaf0ef); (3) add nav tab item counts from loaded JSON arrays (~10 lines JS); (4) fix /tmp/sorted_pending.json stale-cache bug at analyze_batch.py:720 (delete on startup).
